question: Why does linear interpolation between neuron-aligned independently trained networks still fail, and can matching internal activation statistics repair the path?

key_findings.claim: Aligned but imperfectly correlated endpoint features lose variance when their weights are averaged, and the loss compounds with depth.
key_findings.evidence: For midpoint activations with matched endpoint standard deviations, the first-layer variance is multiplied by 0.5 + 0.5 correlation; the typical reported aligned correlation near 0.4 implies a 30% reduction. Measured activation variance then progressively collapses through MLP, VGG, and ResNet layers while endpoint statistics remain healthy.

key_findings.claim: REPAIR substantially reduces interpolation barriers across architectures, datasets, normalization choices, width, and depth.
key_findings.evidence: After neuron alignment, it sets each interpolated unit's mean and standard deviation to interpolations of endpoint statistics. ResNet18/CIFAR-10 barrier falls from 16% to 1.5%; ResNet50/ImageNet midpoint rises from below 1% accuracy to 56.5%, reported as a 74% relative barrier reduction.

key_findings.claim: The correction is data-dependent calibration, not a pure weight-space symmetry operation.
key_findings.evidence: Exact REPAIR records endpoint means, variances, and covariances on a calibration set; the approximate implementation inserts BatchNorm wrappers and passes roughly 5,000 training examples to estimate statistics before fusing affine corrections. Therefore a claimed low-barrier weight path depends on an auxiliary input distribution.

key_findings.claim: REPAIR does not establish the conjecture that permutation symmetry alone removes loss barriers.
key_findings.evidence: The method is explicitly applied on top of alignment and adds channelwise affine transformations absent from the conjectured permutation. Even after full correction, ImageNet midpoint accuracy remains 56.5%, well below approximately 76% endpoints; unaligned midpoint interpolation is still poor.

key_findings.claim: Normalization architecture changes the baseline dramatically and clarifies an apparent conflict in earlier merging results.
key_findings.evidence: At width 8, a LayerNorm ResNet20 midpoint reaches 90.3% before repair versus 32.3% for BatchNorm, because test-time LayerNorm continually corrects scale while frozen BatchNorm behaves affinely. REPAIR brings them to 93.2% and 94.4%, respectively.

key_findings.claim: The constructive merge evidence is promising but narrow.
key_findings.evidence: In one CIFAR-100 experiment, endpoint models trained on disjoint biased class subsets have REPAIRed interpolation points outperforming either corrected endpoint. The appendix compares output ensembling and a full-data model, but the setting does not cover heterogeneous tasks, architectures, initializations, or modern foundation-model fine-tunes.

method.core_idea: Align hidden units between two independently trained networks, linearly interpolate their weights, then restore each interpolated channel's activation mean and variance to the interpolation of endpoint statistics.
method.mechanism: Use activation-correlation matching for permutations, estimate endpoint/cross-network statistics on calibration data, compute exact per-alpha affine corrections or approximate them by inserted BatchNorm layers, and optionally fuse those layers back into convolutions.
assumptions: Channelwise first- and second-order statistics capture the dominant interpolation failure.
A calibration distribution representative of deployment is available.
Neuron alignment establishes a meaningful channel correspondence.
Affine re-normalization does not destroy useful higher-order or cross-channel structure.
Barrier reduction on same-task vision models transfers to broader merging scenarios.

techniques.role: Permutes endpoint channels into a matched coordinate system.
Tracks channel activation variance layer by layer along the interpolation path.
Uses endpoint variances and covariance to set path-specific affine scales.
Provides an efficient approximate calibration and layer-fusion implementation.
Evaluates worst path degradation across alpha, depth, width, and normalization variants.

evaluations.result: Below 1% rises to 56.5%; reported relative barrier reduction is 74%
evaluations.baseline: Activation matching / weight matching without full REPAIR

evaluations.setting: MLP, VGG, and ResNet sweeps on four image datasets
evaluations.result: REPAIR reduces barriers 60-100% relatively and makes VGG barrier nearly depth-invariant
LayerNorm has a much stronger uncorrected midpoint; correction improves all variants
Some corrected interpolation points outperform either corrected endpoint
evaluations.baseline: Logit ensemble, endpoints, and a model trained on all data

limitations: Correction requires representative calibration inputs and can drift under distribution shift.
It matches only per-channel means and variances, not full feature covariance or higher moments.
Neuron alignment remains essential near the midpoint and is combinatorial/heuristic.
The best ImageNet midpoint is still far below endpoint accuracy, so barriers are reduced rather than eliminated.
Most experiments merge identical architectures trained on the same task and recipe.
No calibration-set-size sensitivity, label-free deployment shift, or total merge-time comparison is central to the study.
The path includes learned affine corrections and therefore is not merely a straight line between permuted weights.
failure_modes: Calibration statistics represent one domain and damage another.
Matched channels have similar correlation but incompatible semantics or covariance.
Cross-channel cancellation survives per-channel variance repair.
A residual branch or normalization boundary omitted from repair continues to collapse.
Merging unrelated tasks creates feature interference rather than only scale loss.
An apparently low accuracy barrier masks badly calibrated probabilities or subgroup degradation.
reusable_insights: Instrument internal feature norms and variances before attributing a merge failure to loss-landscape topology.
Treat post-merge calibration data as part of the algorithm and report its provenance and size.
Compare permutation alignment, statistical correction, and their interaction explicitly.
Residual-block outputs can require correction even when every convolution is calibrated.
Path connectivity and useful model fusion are related but distinct evaluation targets.
open_questions: Can distribution-free or analytically propagated statistics replace calibration data?
Would whitening/recoloring full covariance outperform channelwise repair without overfitting?
How does variance repair scale to Transformers, mixture-of-experts, and task-vector merging?
Can alignment and statistic correction be optimized jointly rather than sequentially?
Which higher-order feature failures remain after variance is restored?
Can one bound downstream loss from layerwise correlation and moment mismatch?

competitive_landscape.title: The Role of Permutation Invariance in Linear Mode Connectivity of Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Poses the permutation-connectivity conjecture and documents depth/width effects; REPAIR identifies activation variance as an additional obstruction and adds calibration.

competitive_landscape.title: Git Re-Basin: Merging Models modulo Permutation Symmetries
competitive_landscape.difference: Develops permutation-coordinate-descent and activation matching for zero-barrier merging; REPAIR is complementary post-alignment moment correction and explains why alignment alone may fail.

competitive_landscape.title: Model Soups: Averaging Weights of Multiple Fine-Tuned Models Improves Accuracy without Increasing Inference Time
competitive_landscape.difference: Averages fine-tunes from a shared initialization, where weights already occupy a common basin; REPAIR targets independently trained, permutation-misaligned endpoints.

competitive_landscape.title: ZipIt! Merging Models from Different Tasks without Training
competitive_landscape.difference: Permits within- and cross-model feature zipping for partially disjoint tasks, broadening beyond REPAIR's mainly same-task two-model interpolation.

competitive_landscape.title: Vanishing Feature: Diagnosing Model Merging and Beyond
competitive_landscape.difference: Generalizes variance collapse into input-feature vanishing, supplies deeper theory, and proposes Preserve-First Merging that targets early-layer features rather than matching every channel statistic.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Variance collapse is a principal barrier after neuron alignment, and restoring interpolated activation statistics makes independently trained vision networks nearly linearly connected.
novelty_assessment.evidence: A first-layer derivation, deep activation diagnostics, extensive architecture/data sweeps, normalization ablations, ImageNet results, and a split-data merge support the mechanism and correction.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The diagnosis is clear, influential, and reusable, and the simple calibration step delivers large gains. It complements rather than proves permutation-only connectivity, and its dependence on calibration data and residual ImageNet barrier are material boundaries.

reviewer_notes: Read all 21 pages, including exact/approximate formulas, implementation, baseline comparison, split-data merging, and unaligned ablation. Direct re-basin, local averaging, heterogeneous merging, and later feature-vanishing work were checked against primary arXiv/PMLR records on 2026-08-23.
